chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 105 — Rejoice, Children of Truth
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness responsibly available for this chapter. No surviving Aramaic manuscript preserves Chapter 105, and the fourth-century Chester Beatty–Michigan Papyrus XII passes directly from Chapter 104 to Chapter 106 without this passage. The translation therefore follows the complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann’s 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, printed page 90. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no wording absent from the Geʽez witness was supplied.

verses.text: In those days the Lord said that they should summon the children of the earth and testify to them with their wisdom: ‘Show it to them, for you are their guides and the recompense over all the earth.
verses.study: The received books of Chapter 104 become a public commission. Wisdom is to summon, testify, and guide rather than remain a private possession.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:5–8 — received wisdom is displayed before the peoples
Daniel 12:3 — those who guide many to righteousness shine

verses.text: For I and my Son will be joined with them forever in the paths of truth during their lives, and peace will be yours. Rejoice, children of truth. Amen.’
verses.study: The brief conclusion anchors righteous instruction in abiding divine fellowship. Truth is a lived path marked by peace and joy.
crossReferences: Psalm 85:10–13 — righteousness, truth, and peace meet along God’s path
John 14:23 — the Father and Son make their dwelling with the one who keeps the word

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 105 is a compact conclusion to the written testimony of Chapters 92–104. The books entrusted to the righteous are not merely to be possessed; their wisdom must be used to summon and instruct the children of the earth.

The teachers are called guides, linking faithful preservation of the text with faithful direction of life. Wisdom carries responsibility: what has been received truthfully must be shown and testified truthfully.

The Lord’s promise joins divine presence to those who walk the paths of truth. The wording preserved in Geʽez names both the Lord and ‘my Son,’ placing enduring fellowship at the center of the promised life.

Peace and joy form the final summons. After long warnings against violence, deception, and oppression, the Epistle closes by addressing ‘children of truth’ whose daily path corresponds to the heavenly record they have received.
